what_happened: The the person running Athena edited the governing brief directly, outside a job. The edit added six sections for 4 to 8 November and had no matching spec entries, so the spec coverage tests failed for every job. The the person running Athena then added the missing spec requirements (mechanism none) by hand, and the xtask tests pass again.
cause: The brief and its paired spec file are kept in step only by a test that runs later, and nothing at edit time ties them together. A direct the person running Athena edit outside a job skips the coverage checks, so the mismatch shows up only when later unrelated jobs fail. Athena also has no path that drafts the spec entries when the brief changes.
prevention: Add a pre-commit or pre-push check, and a command for brief edits, that runs the spec coverage tests on any change to the brief. It should refuse the commit, or generate stub spec entries for the new sections, when entries are missing. A brief change would then never reach main with its spec out of step.
proposed_request: Make brief edits safe to commit outside a job. Outcome: when BRIEF.md changes, the spec coverage check runs before the commit or push is accepted, and it refuses the change if any brief section lacks a spec requirement. Athena should also offer a command that lists the missing sections and writes stub spec entries for them (mechanism none, to be filled in). Acceptance: (1) a brief edit with a new section and no spec entry is refused with a message naming the section; (2) after the stub command runs, the spec tests pass; (3) an unchanged brief is not slowed or refused; (4) the check is demonstrated on a real past brief edit, not only a hand-built one.
